title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Lopez (Redwood SE), Jordan Wu (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (NovaPay Head of ML), Priya Singh (NovaPay Platform Eng), Diego Ramos (NovaPay SRE)
---
[00:00] Speaker 1 (Ethan): Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick agenda — 1) recap last week's changes to batching and queueing, 2) review the throughput dashboard, 3) decide steady-state test window and next steps. Liam / Priya are you good with that?
[00:22] Speaker 2 (Liam): Yeah that works. sorry morning here, had one conflict earlier but we're good.
[00:35] Speaker 3 (Maya): Quick note, we pushed the continuous batching changes to the staging pool yesterday around 2 AM PT, and we also adjusted the concurrency limiter to target 20 concurrent request slots per instance, so you should see different batch size distribution.
[00:50] Speaker 4 (Priya): We saw immediate effect, qps jump but also some p99 spikes during a few hundred-second window, looks like cold-starts or rebalancing?
[01:12] Speaker 3 (Maya): Right so two things: one is tail latency when a new worker spins up and hasn't warmed the KV cache; second is a short burst where the queue overflows and we drop into smaller batches. We're tracking both.
[01:30] Speaker 1 (Ethan): I'll pull up the dashboard — lemme share my screen.
[01:45] Speaker 1 (Ethan): Okay on the perf dashboard you can see baseline (week prior) vs post-change. Baseline avg qps ~420, post-change avg qps ~570, that's about a 35% uplift. Avg latency dropped from ~210ms to 170ms at our typical batch sizes. p99 still around 1.1s in a couple of windows.
[02:10] Speaker 2 (Liam): Can you show batch size distribution — are we seeing many tiny batches? that's usually why p99s climb.
[02:20] Speaker 3 (Maya): Yep — histogram on the right. Before we had a 60% small-batch tail (1-2 tokens/req), now that's down to ~28%, and we have a longer mode around 16-24 requests per batch. There are occasional drops to 1-2 because of the concurrency limiter resetting when a slot expires.
[02:50] Speaker 4 (Diego): What's the queue length threshold — we set queue to 100 in staging right?
[03:00] Speaker 3 (Maya): For this run we set per-instance queue depth to 120 and global pending queue cap is 3k for the cluster. We found that lowering per-instance queue below ~80 increases tiny batches. 120 seems sweet spot for this workload.
[03:18] Speaker 2 (Priya): What about backpressure behavior — do requests get queued at the gateway or at the instance process? we saw some 503s during a rebalance last night.
[03:33] Speaker 3 (Maya): Good question. We queue at the gateway until per-instance queue is reached, then we do a short-circuit and route to another instance if available. 503s we saw were when the entire pool was draining and autoscaler was removing nodes; we added a 30s drain window but during rapid scale-down we can still see a few fails.
[03:52] Speaker 1 (Ethan): Also worth noting that in dedicated mode you can pin capacity to avoid that scale-down noise. For hosted, we can adjust autoscaler thresholds or enable graceful draining.
[04:10] Speaker 2 (Liam): We mostly care about predictable throughput during peak — ideally steady 600 qps with p99 < 800ms. Can we meet that with the current config?
[04:23] Speaker 3 (Maya): Short answer: probably yes with more prewarming + slightly higher concurrency target. We tuned to 20 earlier; pushing to 28-30 concurrency per instance increases throughput but at cost of higher avg latency. We can aim for 600 qps with p99 ~750ms by increasing prewarm and ensuring KV cache hit rate > 85%.
[04:48] Speaker 4 (Diego): KV cache hit rates — what's current?
[04:52] Speaker 3 (Maya): Right now staging showed ~78% KV hits. With a warmup script (we shared last week) we can push that to >90% in a few minutes. The problem is cold starts after deploys or after autoscaler scales to zero for low-traffic windows.
[05:10] Speaker 2 (Priya): Would prewarmed instances avoid the autoscaler shrinking to zero?
[05:18] Speaker 3 (Maya): Yes, you can set a minimum instance count in Dedicated or set a lower scale-to-zero threshold in Hosted tier. For the POC we recommended keeping a small reserve during test runs.
[05:28] Speaker 1 (Ethan): I'll call out the tradeoffs: higher concurrency improves throughput but pushes up avg latency and may increase token-per-second cost. Continuous batching improves unit efficiency but needs a sufficiently deep queue to aggregate requests without blowing up latency.
[05:49] Speaker 2 (Liam): Can you explain the queueing numbers we should tune? like per-instance queue, global window, and concurrency target.
[05:59] Speaker 3 (Maya): Sure — our recommendation for this workload based on traces is: per-instance queue: 110-140, concurrency: 24-30 (depending on target latency), global pending cap: 2k-4k. Start with 120 & 26 concurrency for steady-state test.
[06:20] Speaker 4 (Priya): Any changes required on our side — do we need to change client timeouts?
[06:26] Speaker 3 (Maya): Increase client-side timeouts to 3s during the test so requests aren't cut prematurely; also adopt retry with jitter for 5xx transient fails. We sent a sample client wrapper last week.
[06:40] Speaker 1 (Ethan): Let's walk through the anomaly windows — here at 02:12 UTC we see a p99 spike to 2.3s for about 90s. That's when autoscaler removed a node because of a CPU metric mis-reporting.
[06:57] Speaker 2 (Liam): Mis-reporting? is that on our metrics side?
[07:01] Speaker 3 (Maya): We saw a transient metric blur due to the agent heartbeat delay; we're patching the agent to smooth short gaps. But for you, the mitigation is to keep a min-instance count or extend drain windows.
[07:18] Speaker 4 (Diego): Noted. We'll adjust autoscaler configs for the test window.
[07:25] Speaker 2 (Priya): Any GPU memory or utilization concerns?
[07:29] Speaker 3 (Maya): GPU utilization averaged 63% during the post-change window, with peaks to ~88% during 10s bursts. Memory stayed under 75% thanks to quantized model variant. We can push more throughput by increasing model parallelism or switching to larger instance types but that adds cost.
[07:50] Speaker 1 (Ethan): Cost note: with continuous batching and current infra we'll see token cost improvements because more tokens are amortized per kernel launch. We'll send an estimated delta in the follow-up spreadsheet.
[08:02] Speaker 4 (Liam): About hosted vs dedicated — if we go Dedicated, are we able to fully eliminate autoscale churn?
[08:09] Speaker 3 (Maya): Dedicated gives you pinned capacity and reserved GPUs so you control scale; you'll have fewer surprises. For POC we can run a dedicated mini-pool for the 24h steady-state test if you'd like.
[08:22] Speaker 2 (Priya): That might help with reproducibility. Cost for dedicated during test — can you give a ballpark?
[08:30] Speaker 1 (Ethan): We'll send a scoped price estimate — depends on instance size and duration; ballpark for a small dedicated pool for 24h is in the follow-up.
[08:41] Speaker 2 (Liam): Okay great. On telemetry — can you provide raw logs for the anomaly windows, not just aggregated p99? we want request traces.
[08:51] Speaker 3 (Maya): Yes we'll share the trace samples and raw requests; they may have masked tokens but we include timings and batch ids.
[09:00] Speaker 4 (Diego): One more question — queue backpressure and client retries: if we do retries on 5xx, will that amplify queue pressure?
[09:07] Speaker 3 (Maya): Good call — we recommend exponential backoff + jitter and client-side concurrency limiting. Avoid aggressive retries; better to have clients observe a retry-after header and back off. We can surface the header in the staging env.
[09:22] Speaker 2 (Priya): For the steady-state 24h run, do we need to lock config or can we iterate?
[09:28] Speaker 1 (Ethan): Lock it for the first 2 runs to gather baselines; then iterate. We'll coordinate change windows with you.
[09:36] Speaker 2 (Liam): Sounds good. Anything else on tuning?
[09:41] Speaker 3 (Maya): One micro-opt: enabling a small-ish chunked streaming output mode reduces p50 by ~15ms for token-at-a-time workloads; not huge but helps. Also quantization to int8 gave better memory footprint and allowed higher concurrency.
[09:59] Speaker 4 (Diego): Are there any security/reg compliance blockers for dedicated testing?
[10:03] Speaker 5 (Jordan): For POC Dedicated we need signed NDA addendum for on-prem-like network configs; otherwise we can provide isolated VPC with KMS integration. I'll attach the checklist to the CRM record.
[10:14] Speaker 2 (Priya): Good, attach that please.
[10:16] Speaker 1 (Ethan): Quick recap of concrete next actions — we'll send the perf dashboard and raw logs, propose test windows, share pricing and security docs. Priya/Diego will run the customer-side load-gen and report anomalies.
[10:28] Speaker 2 (Liam): Ok recap noted. Any open risks?
[10:32] Speaker 3 (Maya): Risk: tail latency during scale events and cold starts; mitigation: min-instance, prewarm, extended drain. Operational risk: autoscaler heartbeat glitches — patch in flight.
[10:45] Speaker 1 (Ethan): Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with attachments and schedule.
[10:50] Speaker 2 (Liam): Thanks all.
